review.evidence_summary: Both OL records have the same 1925 first-publish year, overlapping authorship, related subjects, and high-confidence matches to the same Wikidata entity. However, their titles differ substantially and may reflect an original/translated-title relationship, which the packet does not explicitly establish as the same project conceptual work; convergence on one external entity alone is insufficient.

Both Open Library records have the identical title, author key, and first-publish year, and each has a high-confidence SAME assertion to the same accepted Wikidata identity. No conflicting or edition-level relation is indicated.

E000000087 and E000009178 share the same author, 1898 first-publish year, and title differing only by punctuation, supporting safe grouping. E000018788 has the different title “Scouts and comrades”; although all three records have high-confidence matches to one Wikidata entity, that shared external target alone does not establish conceptual identity and may over-aggregate them.

E000005748 and E000006177 share the same title, author, 1934 first-publish year, and high-confidence direct identity assertions to Q318333, supporting duplicate grouping. The other records have differing titles and years (1890, 1896, and 1908); E000011947 explicitly describes a translation and has only a medium-confidence assertion. Although all five point directly to the same Wikidata entity, that convergence alone does not establish one conceptual work across potentially distinct translations.

Both Open Library records have the same title, first-publish year, and subjects, and each has a high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata work entity. The differing Open Library author keys indicate an authorship-record variation rather than a distinct work.

All nine Open Library records have direct high-confidence SAME assertions to one Wikidata entity, and six are independently matched to one Goodreads entity. Their titles are close variants and their author/subject metadata substantially overlaps. However, unexplained first-publish years range from 1904 to 1945, and some records add a second author, so the otherwise well-supported duplicate grouping warrants review.

All five records share the same author and are matched to one Wikidata entity, while titles are close variants. However, translation-related subjects and materially different first-publish years (1900–1944) leave unclear whether these are duplicate records, distinct translations, or differently scoped versions; the shared external entity alone is insufficient to collapse them.

E000000125 and E000019383 have the same title, author, 1947 first-publish year, subjects, and direct matches to both external entities, supporting a duplicate grouping. E000000126 has the same author and overlapping subjects but a different-language title and 1939 year, suggesting a possible original/translation relationship. Shared Goodreads and Wikidata targets do not alone establish project-level conceptual identity across that distinction.

Both Open Library records have the same title, author key, and first-publish year (1949), and each has a high-confidence direct identity assertion to the same Wikidata entity Q7730932. No conflicting or special work relation is indicated.

Both Open Library records have the same author and first-publish year, with titles differing only by the missing space in “recuyellof.” Both also have high-confidence SAME assertions to the same Wikidata entity.

Both Open Library records have the identical title, author key, and first-publish year (1939), and each has a direct high-quality title-and-author match to the same Goodreads entity. No conflicting evidence is supplied.

Both OL records match the same Wikidata entity, but they have different author keys, titles in apparently different languages, and first-publish years (1898 versus 1908). Only E000000148 has a direct Goodreads match. The evidence does not establish whether E000021554 is a translation of the same conceptual work or an external-source overmerge.

Both Open Library records have the same author and close first-publish years, and both are asserted to match Wikidata Q2379553. However, their titles differ substantially, one external match is only medium-confidence, and shared linkage to one external entity does not by itself establish that the Open Library targets are the same conceptual work.

Both OL records have the same author and first-publish year and independently match the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. However, the titles differ by language ("Подросток" and "A raw youth"), and the former record includes a translations-into-English subject. The packet does not establish whether the project should treat the apparent original/translation relationship as one conceptual work.

Both Open Library records have the same author and each has a high-confidence assertion to Wikidata Q124081616, while the longer and shorter titles may be variants. However, convergence on one external entity does not alone establish identity, and the differing first-publish years (1897 versus 1894) are not explained by the packet.

All four OL records map to one Goodreads entity, but that convergence alone does not establish identity. The records have differing titles, materially different first-publish years (1880, 1920, 1927, and 1930), and E000028370 has additional author attributions. Only E000000193 has direct Wikidata support, so the packet does not safely establish a single work or a definitive partition.

The four original-title records share the same primary author, closely matching title variants, compatible subjects, and high-confidence links to the same Wikidata entity; three also converge on the same Goodreads entity. The six 'The downfall' records appear translation-related, but their publication years range from 1892 to 1925 and two add different coauthors. Shared Wikidata linkage alone does not establish whether these are duplicates, distinct translations, or revised versions.

All four records share an author and are matched to the same Wikidata entity, but Goodreads splits the matched records across two entities and does not directly cover E000003479. The titles differ across Russian/transliterated and English forms, one record explicitly has a translations-into-English subject, and first-publish years range from 1900 to 1946. The packet does not establish whether these are duplicate records, translations treated as one work, or distinct related works.

E000000208 and E000014145 share the exact title, 1944 first-publish year, closely overlapping subjects, and high-confidence matches to the same Wikidata entity, supporting safe grouping despite an authorship variation. E000000210 and E000029161 have related but different titles and materially different years (1928 and 1899); their convergence on the same Wikidata entity does not alone establish conceptual identity, and only E000029161 has a Goodreads match.

All three Open Library records have the same title or a punctuation variant, share author OL4326986A, have substantially overlapping subjects, and each has a direct high-auto-match SAME assertion to Goodreads entity E000039947. OL44302107W adds a second author. The differing first-publish years (1908, 1924, and 1927) are unexplained and prevent high confidence.

E000000214 and E000002157 share the same title, author, 1948 year, closely matching subjects, and direct SAME assertions to both Goodreads and Wikidata, supporting safe grouping. E000003372 has a different author and 1950 year and is linked only to the shared Wikidata entity; that common external link alone does not establish identity and may reflect over-aggregation.

All three OL records share the title "Loving" and independently match the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities, but this convergence alone does not establish identity. The records include different author keys, and E000000216 has a 1949 first-publish year versus 1945 for the other two; the packet does not explain these discrepancies. No subset can be grouped safely from the supplied evidence.

All three Open Library records have the title “Nothing,” the same 1950 first-publish year, and direct high-quality SAME assertions to Goodreads 122220 with WORK_FULL title and EXACT_NAME author matching. The differing Open Library author keys are consistent with an authorship-record variation, and there is no conflicting external or structural evidence.

All four Open Library records have the same author key and closely corresponding Russian/English titles, and each is directly matched to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. However, the English-title records have materially later first-publish years (1927, 1933, and 1949 versus 1880), and translation evidence is present, so the collapse requires review.

All three OL records have the identical title, strongly overlapping subjects concerning panic and radio broadcasting, and separate high-confidence SAME assertions to the same Wikidata entity. However, one record has a different author key and the 1947 first-publish year differs from the other records' 1940 year, so the duplicate interpretation is not entirely straightforward.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and first-publish year (1950), and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity via AUTO_MATCH_HIGH with exact-name author matching and to the same Wikidata entity via high-confidence judgments. The differing Open Library author keys appear to be record-level attribution variation, with no conflicting evidence supplied.

Both Open Library records have the same author and are matched to the same Wikidata entity, but their titles differ ('Angústia' and 'Anguish') and their first-publish years are 1936 and 1946. This materially suggests a possible original/translation relationship, which the packet does not explicitly resolve under the project's conceptual-work policy; only the 1936 record also has a direct Goodreads match.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and first-publish year (1936), and each is directly matched to the same Goodreads entity and the same Wikidata entity. The Goodreads matches report full-title and exact-author-name agreement; the differing Open Library author keys therefore appear to be attribution-record variation rather than evidence of distinct works.

Both Open Library records have the title “The timeless land” and first-publish year 1941. Each independently has a high-quality SAME assertion to the same Goodreads entity and a high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity. The differing Open Library author keys are best treated as authorship-record variation given the otherwise consistent direct evidence.

Both Open Library records have the identical title, author key, and first publication year (1950), with overlapping subjects. Each also has a direct high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity Q97860845, with no conflicting evidence in the packet.

All three Open Library records have the identical title and 1921 first-publish year. Each independently matches the same Goodreads entity with AUTO_MATCH_HIGH and EXACT_NAME evidence, and each also directly matches the same Wikidata entity. The differing Open Library author keys are consistent with duplicate author attribution records, with no supplied evidence of distinct works or external-source conflict.

All three Open Library records share the title and similar subjects and independently match one Goodreads entity, but that convergence alone does not prove identity. E000000271 has a different author key from the other two, while E000009978 has a materially different first-publish year (1929 versus 1916) with no explanation in the packet.

All three Open Library records have the same title and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities; the matching evidence reports full-title matches and compatible or exact author names. However, the records use two author keys and have unexplained first-publish years of 1924, 1927, and 1929, reducing confidence.

Both Open Library records have the same author and titles differing only in capitalization, and each independently matches the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. The materially different first_publish_year values (1894 and 1912) are unexplained, reducing confidence.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and author key, and each is directly matched to the same Goodreads entity and the same Wikidata entity. The first-publish years differ only slightly (1926 versus 1927), with no evidence of a distinct version or work.

Both Open Library records have the same title and author key, and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. The one-year first-publish discrepancy (1942 versus 1943) is minor and no conflicting grouping evidence is present.

All three Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization, the same first-publish year (1946), and closely aligned horse/ranch subjects. Each is directly matched to the same Goodreads entity with exact-name/high automatic matching and independently to the same Wikidata entity with high confidence. The differing Open Library author key on E000014125 is best treated as authorship-record variation given the otherwise consistent direct evidence.

Both Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization and the same first-publish year (1939). Each is directly matched with high-strength evidence to the same Goodreads entity and, independently, to the same Wikidata entity. The differing author keys indicate an authorship-record variation but no material conflict is supplied.

Both Open Library records share the title The Cardinal and independently map to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. However, they have different author keys and materially different first-publish years (1914 versus 1950); the profile identifies only a same-title pattern. The external convergence therefore does not safely establish conceptual identity and may reflect external over-aggregation.

Both Open Library records have the same author and subjects and are directly matched to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. However, their titles differ ("The woman of Rome" versus "La Romana") and their first-publish years differ (1949 versus 1947), suggesting a possible translation/original-title relationship that the packet does not explicitly resolve under the project's identity policy.

All three Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization, the same 1941 first-publish year, and closely overlapping fiction and motion-picture-industry subjects. Each also has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity with exact-name/full-title matching and to the same Wikidata entity with high-confidence judgments. The differing author key on E000000319 is consistent with an authorship-record variation rather than evidence of a distinct work.

Both Open Library records have the identical title, author key, and first-publish year (1948). Each also has a direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH identity assertion, based on exact author and full-title matches, to the same Goodreads entity, with no conflicting evidence in the packet.

Both Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization, the same first-publish year (1947), and compatible subject metadata. Each is directly matched to the same Goodreads entity and the same Wikidata work entity; the Wikidata matches are high-confidence, and the Goodreads matches use full-title evidence. The differing author attribution is consistent with record variation rather than evidence of distinct works.

Both Open Library records have the same author and first-publish year (1902), closely corresponding titles, and substantially overlapping subjects. Each also has a high-confidence direct identity assertion to the same Wikidata entity, supporting treatment as duplicate records for one conceptual work.

E000000353 and E000003912 share the same author, closely variant titles, and direct SAME assertions to both the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. E000021368 has a 1945 first-publish year, an additional author, a distinct German title, and the subject 'adaptations'; it matches the shared Wikidata entity but has no direct Goodreads match, suggesting Wikidata may have over-aggregated an adaptation with the underlying work.

Eight records share the title “Heidi,” the same primary author, and substantially overlapping subjects; their direct Wikidata matches support grouping despite varied first-publish years and one added coauthor. E000004055 instead has the distinct title “Shirley Temple in Heidi,” a 1937 year, and only a medium-confidence match to the shared Wikidata entity, leaving a possible adaptation or external overmerge unresolved.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and author key, and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. However, their first_publish_year values differ materially (1938 versus 1947) without an explanation in the packet.

The records share an author and 1940 first-publish year but have materially different titles. Both match the same Wikidata entity, while only E000000394 has a Goodreads match; convergence on one external entity alone does not establish that the Open Library targets are the same conceptual work.

All four OL records have high-confidence direct SAME assertions to Wikidata Q8269 and share one author, but this convergence alone does not prove mutual identity. The records use original-language and English title forms, two include translation-related subjects, and first-publish years vary from 1900 to 1935 without an explanation of whether these are translations, editions, or duplicate work records.

Both Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization, the same 1946 first-publish year, strongly overlapping subjects, and independent high-quality title-and-author matches to the same Goodreads work. The differing Open Library author keys appear to be attribution-record variation rather than evidence of distinct works.

The three Open Library records have substantially different titles and materially different first-publish years (1931, 1919, and 1923), despite sharing an author. Their convergence on one Wikidata entity rests on medium-confidence matches and does not establish identity; the Goodreads match applies directly only to E000000411.

All five OL records have matching or subtitle-variant titles, substantially overlapping subjects, and direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities; the Goodreads matches also report exact author-name matches. However, one OL record uses a different author key and the first-publish years range from 1902 to 1912 without an explanation in the packet, reducing confidence.

All three Open Library records have the same title, author key, and first publication year (1942), with closely aligned subjects. Each also has a direct high-quality SAME assertion to the same Goodreads entity, based on exact author and full-work title matches, with no conflicting evidence in the packet.

The records have different titles and materially different first-publish years (1924 versus 1913). Both are matched to one Wikidata entity, but only OL1064267W has a Goodreads match, and shared external identity alone does not establish conceptual identity. The English/French titles and the translation subject on OL1064267W suggest a possible translation or title relationship that the packet does not resolve safely.

E000000440 and E000023036 share the same title, 1946 first-publish year, subject, and Wikidata target, with only expanded authorship on E000023036, supporting a duplicate grouping. E000000448 and E000034011 have different titles and materially different years (1906 and 1910), and each maps to a different Goodreads entity while all four records map to one Wikidata entity. The translation subject on E000000448 and the cross-source disagreement make the relationships unsafe to resolve automatically.

All three OL records share an author and have high-resolution SAME assertions to one Goodreads entity, but their titles differ, translation-related subjects appear on the 1907 records, and E000033627 has a materially later first-publish year (1910). Only E000000446 is linked to Wikidata. The packet does not directly establish whether these are title/translation variants or whether Goodreads has over-aggregated distinct works.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and 1933 first-publish year, and each independently has high-strength SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity and the same Wikidata entity. The differing Open Library author keys are the only material variation, while both Goodreads matches report exact author-name matches.

Both Open Library records have the same author, 1923 first-publish year, and subjects; their titles differ only by the subtitle “a parable.” Each also has a high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity Q7775560. The packet contains no conflicting evidence.

Both Open Library records have the exact title The Manxman, the same first-publish year (1894), compatible fiction subjects, and separate high-confidence SAME assertions to Wikidata Q7750242. The differing Open Library author keys indicate an attribution-record variation but no material work-level conflict is supplied.

Both Open Library records have the same title, author key, and first publication year (1883). Each also has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity and the same Wikidata entity, with no conflicting evidence in the packet.

Both Open Library records have the same title, author key, and first publication year (1927), and each has a high-confidence direct SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity Q7737517. No conflicting evidence is supplied.

E000000528 and E000005632 have near-identical titles, the same 1890 first-publish year, overlapping subjects, and high-confidence links to the same Wikidata entity, supporting safe grouping despite differing author keys. E000005626 adds “for boys,” has a 1918 first-publish year, and only a medium-confidence external match, leaving open whether it is the same work or a revised juvenile version.

All four Open Library records have the same title and author key, closely aligned subjects, and first-publication years of 1896–1897. Each also has a separate high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity, with no conflicting or split evidence in the packet.

All four Open Library records have the same title, author key, and first-publish year, and each has a direct high-quality Goodreads SAME assertion to the same external entity using exact author-name and full-title matches. No conflicting external grouping or material metadata discrepancy is supplied.

All four records share the exact title, 1904 first-publish year, overlapping subjects, and medium-confidence matches to one Wikidata entity. However, three different Open Library author keys are present, and convergence on the same external entity does not alone establish identity; the packet provides no direct evidence resolving the authorship variation.

All four Open Library records have the same title, author key, first-publish year, and subjects. Each also has a direct high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity, with no conflicting evidence or material discrepancy in the packet.

The Open Library records have different titles and first-publish years ("Scaramouche," 1921; "Scaramouche the king-maker," 1931) and map to separate Goodreads entities, but both map to the same Wikidata entity. This cross-source disagreement does not safely establish either identity or distinctness.

The records have the same title and each has a high-confidence match to the same Wikidata entity, but this convergence alone does not establish OL-to-OL identity. Their author attribution differs, and the materially different first-publish years (1893 and 1908) are unexplained.

All three Open Library records have the identical title, closely aligned 1948–1949 first-publish years, overlapping fiction and World War II subjects, and direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH assertions to the same Goodreads work using full-title and exact-name matches. The differing Open Library author keys appear to be attribution-record variation rather than evidence of distinct works.

All three Open Library records have the same title (with only capitalization variation), overlapping subject matter, and separate high-confidence SAME assertions to the same accepted Wikidata entity. The 1900/1901 records also share the same author. The 1920 record has additional author attributions and a materially later first-publish year, reducing confidence despite the otherwise strong convergence.

Both Open Library records have the same title and first-publish year, share author OL32541A, and independently match the same Goodreads entity via high-quality exact-author/full-title assertions and the same Wikidata entity via high-confidence assertions. The second record only adds an additional author attribution.

Both Open Library records have medium-confidence links to the same Wikidata entity, but that convergence alone does not establish identity. Their titles, subject profiles, authorship metadata, and first-publish years (1946 versus 1896) differ, with no direct evidence explaining the discrepancies.

Both Open Library records have the same author key and first-publish year, closely matching titles, and overlapping subjects. Each is directly matched with AUTO_MATCH_HIGH evidence to the same Goodreads entity; one match is WORK_FULL and the other BOOK_FULL, supporting straightforward duplicate/title variation.

Both Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization, the same 1892 first-publication year, and identical subjects. Both are asserted SAME to Wikidata Q2638255, though one assertion is only medium confidence; their author keys differ, and both are classified as translations into English.

The records share the title "Parzival" and each has a high-confidence identity assertion to the same Wikidata entity, but this convergence alone does not prove they are the same conceptual work. They have different Open Library author keys and unexplained first-publish years of 1885 and 1888; the packet provides no direct evidence resolving those differences.

All five Open Library records have the identical title and author key, closely overlapping subjects, and direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. They are best treated as duplicate work records, though the unexplained first-publish-year variation from 1882 to 1885 lowers confidence.

Both Open Library records have the same author key and titles differing only in capitalization, and each has a direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH identity assertion to the same Goodreads work. The unexplained first-publish-year discrepancy (1881 versus 1944) prevents high confidence.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and author key, and each is directly matched to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. The unexplained first-publish-year difference (1881 versus 1884) prevents high-confidence automatic aggregation.

The 1925/1929 first-publication-year difference is modest and does not outweigh the direct title and metadata alignment.

All three Open Library records have the same author key, 1944 first-publish year, fiction subject, and title differing only by terminal punctuation. Each also has a direct high-quality SAME assertion to the same Goodreads entity, with WORK_FULL title matching and no conflicting evidence.

Both Open Library records have the same author and titles differing only in capitalization, and each has a high-confidence direct SAME assertion to Wikidata Q42184818. However, their first_publish_year values differ (1942 versus 1947) without an explanation in the packet, reducing confidence.

Both Open Library records have the exact title "Jim Davis," the same author key, substantially overlapping subjects, and separate high-quality title-and-author matches to the same Goodreads entity. The unexplained first_publish_year discrepancy (1900 versus 1911) prevents high confidence.

All three Open Library records have the same distinctive full title and closely aligned subjects, and each has a direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH Goodreads identity assertion with EXACT_NAME author matching to the same external entity. The 1914/1915 first-publication-year difference is minor, and the differing Open Library author keys are consistent with catalog-level authorship variation.

The records share an author and both match the same Wikidata entity, but they have different-language titles and materially different first-publish years (1900 versus 1932). Only E000034060 has a Goodreads match. The packet does not establish whether this is a translation relationship, duplicate records, or Wikidata over-aggregation, so collapsing them is unsafe.

All four Open Library records have the identical title and author key, and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity and the same Wikidata entity. Their differing first-publish years (1880, 1884, 1894, and 1900) are not explained in the packet, so the otherwise strong duplicate-record interpretation warrants review.

Both Open Library records have the same author, closely related short and expanded titles, overlapping gold-mining fiction subjects, and independent high-confidence SAME assertions to Wikidata Q139674803. The 1884/1885 first-publication-year difference is minor and does not outweigh the direct identity evidence.

All three Open Library records have the same base title and subjects, and each has a high-confidence direct SAME assertion to Wikidata Q1256435. One title adds an English subtitle, and author attribution uses two Open Library author keys. The unexplained 1889 versus 1899 first-publish-year discrepancy prevents high confidence.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and are directly matched to the same Goodreads entity with AUTO_MATCH_HIGH exact-name/full-title evidence and to the same Wikidata entity with high-confidence judgments. However, their author keys differ and their first-publish years are 1897 and 1904, so the apparent duplicate relationship is not entirely straightforward.

E000001038, E000001040, and E000001047 share the same author, subjects, 1898 first-publish year, and matching or expanded titles, supporting duplicate/title-variant grouping. E000009763 has the same author, subjects, and title and independently matches the same Wikidata entity, but its materially different 1905 first-publish year is unexplained; shared external identity alone is insufficient to collapse it safely.

All three Open Library records have the same author, effectively identical titles, overlapping fiction/history subjects, and high-confidence direct matches to the same Wikidata entity. However, OL43118035W has first_publish_year 1913 while the other two have 1908, and the packet does not explain that discrepancy.

Both Open Library records have the same author, share the core title “Peter Trawl,” and independently have high-confidence SAME assertions to Wikidata Q124092730; the longer title appears to add a subtitle. However, the differing first-publish years (1882 and 1890) are unexplained, so the merge is not safe for automatic acceptance.

The records share the same title and author and each has a medium-confidence identity assertion to the same Wikidata entity, but that convergence alone does not establish identity. Their first-publish years differ materially (1882 versus 1887), with no supplied explanation, so a safe collapse is not supported.

E000001117 ('Feu') and E000033624 ('Le feu') share the same author, near-identical titles, adjacent publication years, and direct matches to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities, supporting safe grouping as title variants. E000014226 ('Under fire') has the same author and external matches, but its English title and the translation-related subjects on 'Feu' materially suggest a translation relationship; the packet does not establish that translations should be the same project conceptual work.

Both Open Library records have the same title, author key, first-publish year, and subject, and each has a high-confidence direct SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity. No conflicting evidence is present.

Both Open Library records have the same two-part title with only punctuation variation, share author OL115050A, and independently match Goodreads 296213 through high-quality full-title and exact-name assertions. However, the second record adds another author, and the unexplained first-publication years differ materially (1895 versus 1928); the title also appears to describe a combined work.

Both Open Library records have the identical title "Celia," the same author key, substantially overlapping subjects, and direct high-quality title-and-author matches to the same Goodreads work. The 1937/1938 first-publish-year difference is minor and does not outweigh the direct matching evidence.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and author key, and each has a direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH, BOOK_FULL Goodreads identity assertion to the same Goodreads entity. The unexplained first-publish-year difference (1934 versus 1950) prevents high confidence and automatic acceptance.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and 1946 first-publish year, and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. The differing Open Library author keys appear to be authorship-record variation rather than evidence of distinct works.

Both OL records have the title "My son, my son" and independently match the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities, but shared external targets alone do not prove identity. The records have different author keys and materially different first-publish years (1944 versus 1936), with no supplied evidence explaining those discrepancies.

Both Open Library records have the same author key and first-publish year (1894), with titles differing only in punctuation/diacritics. Both also have high-confidence SAME assertions to the same Wikidata entity, with no conflicting evidence in the packet.

Both Open Library records have the same title, author key, and first publication year (1947), and both directly match the same Goodreads entity through AUTO_MATCH_HIGH assertions based on exact author names and full work titles. No conflicting evidence is supplied.

However, “The Heritage of Dedlow Marsh and Other Tales” may be a collection containing the separately titled work, or merely an expanded title variant. The shared external identity alone does not resolve this possible part/whole relationship.

Both records share an author and 1892 first-publish year and independently match the same Wikidata entity, but that convergence alone does not establish identity. The titles may be variants, yet “Colonel Starbottle's client, and some other people” may denote a collection containing or otherwise related to “Colonel Starbottle's Client”; the supplied evidence does not resolve this possible part/whole relationship.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and author key, and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads and Wikidata entities. The differing first_publish_year values (1885 and 1900) are unexplained, reducing confidence despite otherwise strong convergence.

Both Open Library records have the same author, closely matching titles differing only by the initial article, overlapping fiction/mining subjects, and separate high-confidence SAME assertions to the same Wikidata entity. The unexplained first-publish-year difference (1897 versus 1900) prevents high confidence.

Both point to the same Wikidata entity, but that shared mapping does not establish conceptual identity and appears to overmerge the part with the whole. Both Open Library records have the identical title and 1947 first-publish year, and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity and the same Wikidata entity. The differing author keys and subject profiles indicate catalog variation but no supplied evidence of distinct works.

However, their first-publish years differ materially (1903 versus 1914), and the packet does not explain that discrepancy; convergence on one external entity alone is insufficient to establish identity.

All three OL records have the same or article-variant title, overlapping fiction/Jacobite Rebellion subjects, and direct high-confidence matches to the same Wikidata entity; two also independently match the same Goodreads entity.
